verdict.rationale: Docs describe automatic session persistence to disk, resuming with full prior context (files read, decisions made), forking sessions, and a SessionStore adapter for mirroring transcripts to custom backends so sessions can resume across hosts — directly supporting checkpoint/resume durability. However, this is framed around normal session continuation rather than explicit crash-recovery guarantees, and there's no independent/hands-on evidence confirming exact-resume fidelity after an abrupt crash mid-tool-call. Missing for 10: explicit crash-recovery semantics/guarantees, evidence of mid-tool-call state capture, and independent corroboration of resume behavior after failure.
